extra.message: parseFile() builds a shell command by string-concatenating fileName, arg1 and arg2 (line 22) and runs it via child_process.exec (line 23). All three values originate from the request URL (see routes/php.js) and are never shell-escaped or validated, so a request such as /order.php?item=;id&price=1 injects arbitrary OS commands. This is OS command injection.

The *.php route extracts item, price and path directly from request.originalUrl (lines 20-22) and passes them unvalidated and unescaped to execPHP.parseFile() (lines 31-34), which concatenates them into a child_process.exec shell command in execphp.js:22. Attacker-controlled query parameters (e.g. item=';id') and the .php file path reach an OS command execution sink.

The XML loaded by this file (executed by the Node router via GET /test.php) declares an external entity 'own' referencing file:///etc/passwd, and loadXML() is called with LIBXML_NOENT | LIBXML_DTDLOAD while libxml_disable_entity_loader(false) enables external entity resolution. The expanded entity is echoed back, disclosing arbitrary local file contents. This is XML External Entity (XXE) processing.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: Login queries MongoDB with raw body values: collection.findOne({ username: req.body.username, password: req.body.password }). Because express.json() and urlencoded({extended:true}) (app.js:36-37) parse nested JSON/objects, an attacker can send {"username":{"$ne":""},"password":{"$ne":""}} to inject query operators and log in as the first user without valid credentials (NoSQL injection / authentication bypass).

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: GET /users/userlist performs no authentication or authorization check and returns the full userlist collection, including plaintext password, credit card, email and other personal fields for every user. Anyone can read all registered users' credentials and sensitive data.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: DELETE /users/deleteuser/:id has no authentication/authorization and removes any user document by attacker-supplied id (obtainable from the unauthenticated /userlist endpoint). Any anonymous attacker can delete arbitrary users including admin accounts — broken access control / IDOR.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: POST /users/adduser is intended as an admin-only action (the Add-User UI lives on /admin) but is completely unauthenticated. It inserts the entire request body into the userlist collection with no validation, letting anyone create arbitrary accounts and inject attacker-controlled content (including script payloads in username/email/fullname) that is later rendered by the admin panel, enabling stored XSS.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: populateTable() builds an HTML string by concatenating user-controlled fields (this.username, this.email, this._id) fetched from /users/userlist and injects it into the DOM via $('...').html(tableContent) (line 46) on the /admin page. Because usernames/emails are attacker-controlled and adduser is unauthenticated, this is stored DOM XSS executing in the admin's browser (e.g. a username containing <script>alert(document.cookie)</script>).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

extra.message: State-changing endpoints (PUT /users/modify, DELETE /users/session, etc.) rely solely on session cookies with no CSRF token and no SameSite attribute on the session cookie (app.js:28-33). A malicious page can forge cross-site requests against an authenticated victim to modify their account data or log them out (CSRF).

PUT /users/modify applies the entire request body as $set ({ $set: query }) to the current user's document, with no allow-list of modifiable fields. A user can modify arbitrary own-record attributes (including 'username'), enabling username collisions that can let one account overwrite or impersonate another user's record (mass assignment / insecure direct field update).

The express-session signing secret is a hardcoded, publicly visible value ('Shh, its a secret!'). Anyone who knows it can forge/sign session cookies; it should come from a secure environment variable.

The error handler exposes err.message and, whenever NODE_ENV is not explicitly set to 'production' (bin/www never sets it, so Express defaults to 'development'), the full error object/stack is rendered to the client via views/error.jade. This leaks internal stack traces, file paths and potentially user-supplied error text (CWE-209 / CWE-200).

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
